chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Basri, from Fuzalat ibn Ayyub and Wahb ibn Hafs, from Shahab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, al-Zubayr entered upon the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) with a quince in his hand. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'O Zubayr, what is this in your hand?' He replied: 'O Messenger of God, this is a quince.' He said: 'O Zubayr, eat quinces, for in them are three characteristics.' He said: 'What are they, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'They warm the heart, make the miser generous, and embolden the coward.'

The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: I heard our elder Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrate that al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Zubayr remained from us, the Ahl al-Bayt, until his son (offspring) grew up and turned him away from our opinion.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the three spiritual and physical benefits of eating quinces according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* elucidates the spiritual and physical virtues of quinces, linking their consumption to the purification of the heart, the curing of miserliness, and the bolstering of courage. The compiler’s concluding remark provides crucial historical context, suggesting that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam remained within the fold of the Ahl al-Bayt until his son, Abd Allah, influenced him to diverge in the political disputes following the Prophet's death.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-199 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Basry, on the authority of Fuzalat ibn Ayoob and Wahab ibn Hafs, on the authority of Shahab ibn Abdeh Rab’beh that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

Zubayr had a quince in his hand and went to see God’s Prophet (MGB). The Prophet (MGB) said, ‘O Zubayr! What is this in your hand?’ Then he replied, ‘O Prophet of God! This is a quince.’ Then the Prophet (MGB) said, ‘O Zubayr! Eat quinces since they have three good characteristics.’ Zubayr said, ‘O Prophet of God ! What are they?’The Prophet (MGB) replied, ‘They will warm up the heart, make a miser benevolent and turn a coward into a bold person.’

The compiler of the book - may God be pleased with him - says, “I heard my elder Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrate that As-Sadiq (MGB) said, ‘Zubayr was one of us until his son Abdullah grew up and turned him against us.’”
